A bay in Lake Macquarie adjacent to Galgabba Point and Parbury Park reserve, .5 km west of Old Pacific Hwy, Swansea South.
ORIGIN: Old Margaret, known as the 'last' of the Lake Macquarie district Awabakal aboriginal tribe (Margaret was the wife of 'Ned' who gave his name to Lake Macquarie's Black Ned's Bay and Black Ned's Point). Margaret lived in a small hut on what is now known as 'Parbury Park' until her death at Newcastle hospital in the year 1900.

DESCRIPTION: A bay adjacent to Richards Point within Lake St Clair.
ORIGIN: Part of Singleton Shire Council's naming of geographical features around the Lake St Clair area. Named after the Moore family.
HISTORY: The Moore family was displaced when the Lake filled in the mid 1980's.

DESCRIPTION: A port within Port Jackson about 4 km S of Crows Nest. This feature is dual named.
ORIGIN: Tumbalong is the Aboriginal name for Darling Harbour. The name was chosen in consultation with Sydney Aboriginal communities.

DESCRIPTION: A small bay within Nelson Lagoon approx 1 km WNW of Baronda Head.
A bay situated approx 1 km NNE of Dori Bay and about 1 km S of Penders Beach.
A bay containing Shelly Beach located between Dammerels Head and Look At Me Now Headland near the suburb of Signal Hill.
A bay situated 500m E of Winererremy Bay and 250m S of Old Mangrove Bay at Pittwater in the suburb of Mona Vale.
A small bay located 200m S of Cottage Point near the confluence of Coal and Candle Creek and Cowan Creek in the locality of Cottage Point
ORIGIN: Recognises the long standing association of four generations of Pratt family to Church Point.  Violet and George Pratt purchased Por 3 DP 11177 in June 1932 as part of the subdivision of James Terrey's original 1879 Crown land grant of 100 acres.The family has helped with the public water supply in the 1970s and continue to maintain the Bay.

DESCRIPTION: For a bay located to the west of Bombo Headland and south east of Cathedral Rocks in the locality of Bombo.
ORIGIN: The bay is fronted by rocks and reefs and is a well-documented surfing location.

DESCRIPTION: An inlet on the eastern shore of Lake Wallace approx 315m north of Rocky Waterhole Drive in the locality of Wallerawang.
ORIGIN: According to historian Jim Smith, James Walkers cousin Thomas Archer came to know and respect Myles ('King' Miles or My-ill) who was an Aboriginal leader in the Wallerawang district
